author: PCarme
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**
PTN000112207 (PTHR11035) and PTN000125390 (PTHR11157)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):** 
SPBC19C2.15c/phs1, SPAC1639.01c/elo1, SPAC1B2.03c/elo2

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**
Erroneous source I think. These 3 genes have anntations to 'sphingolipid biosynthetic process' propagated via paint, but they actually function in fatty acid elongation to very-long chain fatty acids, which happens upstream of sphingolipid biosynthesis (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24753812/).
All the experimental annotations to sphingolipid biosynthesis for orthologs of these 3 genes are based on phenotypes of sphingolipid synthesis defects, which appear to be a consequence of impaired FA elongation.
title: PAINT issue: Genes involved in very-long chain fatty acid synthesis annotated to downstream process

author: marcfeuermann
body: There are many primary annotations from yeast to human. It is indeed upstream, so yes, let's remove it.
